finding: Alabama's deer-season geography, read from the authority's own rule
authority: Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, Division of Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries

instrument.citation: Alabama Administrative Code r. 220-2-.01, Hunting Seasons and Bag Limits
instrument.author: Christopher M. Blankenship

currency.evidence: The season table in this same rule states dates for 2024-2025 ("October 15, 2024 - February 10, 2025"), so this is the 2024-25 filing of 220-2-.01, not the rule in force for 2026-27.
currency.consequence: No season date, bag limit or hour from this document may be encoded as current. The ZONE DEFINITIONS are recorded as this filing's wording and must be re-read against the 2026-27 filing before any zone is served.
currency.whatIsStillEstablished: That Alabama defines its deer zones by linear traverse rather than by a county list, and that its CWD zones are defined by whole counties. A later filing could change the lines; it cannot retroactively make this filing a county-composition model.

extraction.method: Flate streams decompressed from the PDF and PostScript show-text strings concatenated; no OCR.
extraction.knownLimitation: The PDF loses the space at each line break, so the extracted strings contain run-together words ("followingboundaries"). The text below is therefore a MECHANICAL EXTRACTION, not a clean transcription: it is evidence of what the rule says and must not be presented as the authority's typography. The authoritative wording is the document at the URL above.
extraction.notRepaired: No space has been inserted and no word re-split. Editing the extraction to look like a quotation would make a North Ground artefact indistinguishable from the authority's own words.

trailingEnumeratorTrimmed.why: The next numbered item's own enumerator ran into the end of the extracted string. Removing it deletes an artefact of this extraction, not a word of the rule; it is recorded here so the deletion is visible rather than invisible.

whyThisMatters: The previously recorded route for Alabama was "ADMINISTRATIVE_COMPOSITION or DERIVED_FROM_DEFINITION from the regulation's own words". The words rule the first out for Zones A-E: the Zone A line runs along US Hwy. 80 through the middle of Sumter and Dallas Counties, so composing the zone from whole counties would be fabrication, not a simplification. Third-party summaries describe Zone B as a county list "with parts of Houston and Henry counties also included", which is the same error already in circulation.

cwdZones.note: "The CWD Management Zone (CMZ) includes all of Lauderdale, Colbert, and Franklin Counties" is resolvable today with the Census county resolver and nothing else. The High-Risk and Buffer Zones inside it cut Franklin County along State Hwy. 24 and US Hwy. 43, so they are a part-county and are not.

familiesExercisedByThisOneInstrument.evidence: Bobcat, coyote, feral swine, fox, beaver/nutria/groundhog, starling/crow/house sparrow, woodcock, snipe, rails and bullfrog are stated with no zone at all; bear, mountain lion and ruffed grouse are stated as "No Open Season".
The CWD Management Zone is three whole counties.
Zones C, D and E are "[t]hose areas of [named counties] with the following boundaries: ..." - a county base cut by a traverse.
Zone A is a closed circuit of highways, rivers and state lines.
Zone B is "[t]hose areas south or west of a line described as: ..." - a half-plane, not a closed polygon.
Zone E is two disjoint areas, each its own county base and traverse.
The CMZ contains the High-Risk Zone and the Buffer Zone, which partition it.

The dog-deer restrictions are county-keyed with intra-county exceptions - CHOCTAW "(that area south of AL Hwy. 10 and west of AL Hwy. 17 and north of County Road 18 ...)" - and name individual-landowner exceptions in Chambers and Coosa.

The sandhill crane season has its own zone, "that area North of Interstate 20 from the Georgia state line to the interchange with Interstate 65, then East of Interstate 65 to the interchange with Interstate 22, then North of Interstate 22 to the Mississippi state line. Excludes the remainder of the state."

priorMeasurementUnchanged: No ADCNR GIS publishes this geography: 47 root services on the authority's own server and nine in SWAP hold no season zone, its recorded service has one layer of properties, and ArcGIS Online returned zero for three phrasings against a positive control of 176 hits elsewhere (measured 2026-10-06). The route is derivation from this text, not acquisition.
